content: As we can see from Table TABREF31, for 20 target words in English there are 24 lemmas, and for 18 target words in Russian there are 36 different lemmas. These numbers are explained by occasional errors in the UDPipe lemmatization. Another interesting thing to observe is the number of distinct word forms for every language. For English, there are 39 distinct forms for 20 target nouns: singular and plural for every noun, except `atmosphere' which is used only in the singular form. Thus, inflectional variability of English nouns is covered by the dataset almost completely. For Russian, we observe 132 distinct forms for 18 target nouns, giving more than 7 inflectional forms per each word. Note that this still covers only half of all the inflectional variability of Russian: this language features 12 distinct forms for each noun (6 cases and 2 numbers).
